newsitem.title: USA: U.S. backs expanded U.N. Security Council.
newsitem.headline: U.S. backs expanded U.N. Security Council.

text.p: The United States said on Thursday it would support expanding the United Nations Security Council's permanent members from five to 10, including three seats for developing countries from Asia, Africa and Latin America.

After a review, "the United States now agrees...that we ought to have developing countries sit on a permanent basis on the U.N. Security Council as permanent members," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.

That would be in addition to Germany and Japan, which Washington has long backed for permanent membership on the council, the only U.N. body with the power to order use of military force and make other binding decisions.

Burns said the United States would not nominate countries for developing country seats. "We believe that the regions themselves -- the African countries, the Latin countries and the Asian countries -- ought to decide how these seats will be filled. Therefore the United States will not be making any recommendations," he said.
In all, the spokesman said, Washington could support an expansion of the security council to 20 or 21 members, up form the current 15.
The United States formally made its views known to the United Nations Thursday. Burns said the issue was expected to be actively discussed through the next year.
